Front page fields, second card version (transcribed from image; one line hidden by a cut line)
Name; Phone No.; State; LGA; Ward; Settlement.
Gender: Female, Male; CDD Team Code; CDD Phone No.
Child's information: Child Name; Beneficiary ID; State; LGA; Ward; Settlement; CD D Team Code; CDD Phone No.
Child's name: the child's name and surname from the caregiver.
Beneficiary ID: the 12-digit alpha-numeric ID generated by the DIGIT app.
CDD team code and CDD phone number: the team that visited, and the recorder's phone.
Name and phone number of the caregiver.
Complete this record if the child is 1 month to 11 months old.
Year: the year of implementation, e.g. 2026.
Round: 1 or 2 in the year of implementation.
Child's age (months): not more than 11 months.
Dose (ml) and date administered. The app shows the dose when you enter the age.
Complete this record when the child is 12 months (1 year) and above.
Year and round (1 or 2), as above.
Height (cm): measure with the dosing pole and write it in centimetres.
Dose (ml): the app shows it when you enter the height; it matches the dosing pole.
Ask the caregiver about other child health interventions.
Last SMC cycle: tick yes or no.
Last Polio: tick yes or no.
Last malaria vaccine received: use the immunization card.
Measles/rubella vaccine: tick yes or no.
Complete the detachable section accurately, detach it properly, return it and keep it safely in the health facility.
AZM child information: beneficiary ID from the app; first name and surname as above; gender; age.
State, LGA, Ward, Health facility, Settlement.
CDD team code and CDD phone number.
Age-based (1-11 months): year, round, age, dose, date. Height-based (12-59 months): height (cm), dose.
SMC child information (Kebbi State integrated card)
Child's name and Beneficiary ID from the technology app.
CDD team code of the team that gives SPAQ.
Cycles: 1 to 4 in year 1 and year 2.
Age: tick 3 to < 12 months or 12 to 59 months.
Day 2 AQ: the caregiver ticks when the second day dose of amodiaquine is given.
Day 3 AQ: the caregiver ticks when the third day dose of amodiaquine is given.
The Child Record Card is expected to last for 2 years. Caregivers should keep it safely in the household.
Review the health advisory on the back of the card. CDDs should leave their phone numbers on the card. Caregivers can then call them about a suspected ADR (passive ADR monitoring).
